issues.legal_issue: A tenant-protective rent restriction that becomes applicable after a possession decree but before its execution can prevent execution of that decree against a tenant who remains in possession.
material_facts: A possession decree was passed while the premises were outside the area covered by the rent-control regime.
Before execution was completed, the premises came within the regime’s coverage and the tenant remained in possession.
The tenant challenged an order directing delivery of possession under the earlier decree.
issues.conclusion: The later-applicable rent restriction prevented execution of the earlier possession decree against the tenant, so the appeal was allowed and the High Court’s judgment was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Section 21(1) prohibits an order or decree for recovery of possession against a tenant except on the grounds permitted by that provision, and Section 3(r) defines tenant to include a person continuing in possession after termination of the tenancy. Following Mani Subrat Jain v. Raja Ram Vohra, the Court treated a person remaining in possession as protected despite a decree or process that had otherwise ended the tenancy under general property law. Because rent-control legislation is beneficial to tenants, its protection is construed liberally; absent express provision or clear implication to the contrary, a restriction that is prospective in form may displace a landlord’s vested right under a final decree. The Court distinguished Konchada Ramamurty Subudhi v. Gopinath Naik, which concerned the parties’ intention under a compromise decree rather than the legislative purpose of a rent-control provision.

predicates.appeal_concerns_execution_of_prior_posse: The proceeding challenges an order allowing execution of a possession decree made earlier.
predicates.premises_entered_rent_protection_before_: The premises came within a tenant-protective rent regime after the possession decree but before its execution was completed.
predicates.occupant_remained_in_possession_after_te: The occupant continued in possession after the tenancy had otherwise been terminated.
predicates.no_clear_exception_preserves_execution: No express provision or clear implication preserved execution of the earlier decree despite the newly applicable tenant protection.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns execution of an earlier possession decree, the premises entered rent protection before execution, the occupant remained in possession after the tenancy ended, and no clear exception preserves execution, execution of the earlier decree is barred.
